nodes.text: Let $k\geq 2$, and let $f_k(n)$ count the number of solutions to\[n=p_1^k+\cdots+p_k^k,\]where the $p_i$ are prime numbers. Is it true that $\limsup f_k(n)=\infty$?

#979 : [Er65b,p.224] number theory Erdős [Er37b] proved this is true when $k=2$, and also when $k=3$ (but this proof appears to be unpublished).
